name: Platform sneakers

lead: Platform sneakers are casual shoes with a thick sole. They are discussed as an easy, wearable way to look taller.
Platform footwear has recurred in fashion from Venetian chopines to the 1970s and 1990s.

paras: The raised sole lifts the wearer by several centimetres; the gain lasts only while the shoes are on.
Podiatrists and consumer groups have warned that raised soles raise ankle sprain and fall risk, per accounts of 1970s platforms. No studies specific to platform sneakers were found.

lead: Platform sneakers are athletic-style shoes with a thick sole that raises the wearer's height. In height-focused style discussion they are described as an easy way to gain extra inches in a casual shoe.
Platform footwear has a long history, from Venetian zoccoli and chopines to the 1970s glam-rock era and 1990s revival.[1] Typical platform soles measure about 5-10 cm.[1]
No studies of platform sneakers and perceived height or attractiveness were found; the article below relies on general descriptions of platform footwear.

paras: Platforms may have continuous, wedge or block soles in cork, wood, crepe, rubber or plastic.[1] They add height while being more stable than stiletto heels.[1]

Platforms peaked in the early 1970s, with men's platforms worn with flared trousers and popularised by glam rock and disco performers; they faded by 1976 in Europe and the early 1980s in the US.[1] Platform sneakers by Buffalo worn by the Spice Girls helped return platforms to everyday fashion in the late 1990s.[1]
Raising the ankle increases the risk of sprains, and inflexible tall soles led to falls and injuries in the 1970s, prompting podiatrist and consumer warnings.[1]
Style advice aimed at shorter men lists thick-soled shoes among ways to gain apparent height without a visible heel. Proponents also mention that chunky sneakers are currently fashionable.

timeline.event: John Fluevog's Munster platform gains wide exposure.[1]
Platforms return to mainstream fashion, helped by the Spice Girls.[1]
